intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of the world's greatest walks through Fiordland National Park, passing stunning waterfalls, alpine meadows, and dramatic mountain passes. The 53.5km trail takes 4 days and offers breathtaking scenery including the famous Mackinnon Pass at 1154m elevation.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungee jumping site, a 43-metre jump above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. This iconic experience is operated by AJ Hackett and includes the option to touch the water on your jump for an extra thrill.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the legendary Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, winding through ancient beech forests, alpine lakes, and panoramic mountain ridges shared between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The Routeburn Falls section is particularly spectacular.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Join a guided hike on the famous Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers descending into a temperate rainforest. Explore stunning ice caves, seracs, and crevasses with expert guides who provide all necessary equipment including crampons and ice axes.
experiences.location: Franz Josef Glacier Village, West Coast

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungee jump at 134 metres above the remote Nevis River gorge. This extreme freefall lasts 8.5 seconds and reaches speeds of 120km/h, offering unmatched adrenaline and jaw-dropping views of the Central Otago landscape from the suspended cable car pod.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the legendary Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, winding through ancient beech forests, alpine lakes, and panoramic mountain ridges shared between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The Routeburn Falls section is particularly spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange budget transport (shuttle or public bus) to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport arrivals hall or a 24-hour petrol station convenience store near the resort — keep it simple tonight (budget ~NZD $10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book an airport shuttle in advance for the cheapest option (~NZD $20-25 per person). Alternatively, the Christchurch Metro Purple Line bus runs from the airport and is the most budget-friendly option (~NZD $3.50). Confirm your resort's late check-in policy before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, explore the beachfront area near Aegean Bliss Resort on foot. Take a relaxed walk along the shoreline, breathe in the fresh New Zealand air, and get your bearings. Visit a local supermarket (Pak'nSave or Countdown) to stock up on snacks, bread, peanut butter, and fruit for budget meals throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Christchurch city centre (bus or bike share). Visit the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens — 21 hectares of stunning gardens perfect for a gentle stroll. Then explore the Cardboard Cathedral and the Re:START Mall to see the city's post-earthquake resilience. Walk along the Avon River Punting area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Christchurch Night Market (if running on Monday) or explore the nearby suburb of Sumner for a casual seaside evening walk. Return to the resort and plan the rest of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — pick up bread, eggs, and fruit from the supermarket (~NZD $8)
meals.lunch: Pak'nSave or New World supermarket deli — grab a pre-made sandwich or sushi rolls (~NZD $6-8)
meals.dinner: Christchurch's Rolleston Ave food trucks or Hachi Hachi Japanese restaurant for budget ramen (~NZD $15-18)

day_by_day.notes: Get a Christchurch Metro card (Metrocard) for discounted bus fares (~NZD $2 per trip vs $3.50 cash). The Botanic Gardens are completely free. Budget for the day: ~NZD $40-50 total.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the iconic Banks Peninsula hike. Take the bus or a hired car to Akaroa (about 1.5 hours from Christchurch). Begin the Akaroa Head Scenic Reserve walk — a stunning coastal hike with panoramic views of the volcanic harbour, French colonial-style village below, and the Pacific Ocean. The track takes about 2-3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Akaroa on foot — it's free! Walk the waterfront, browse the French-themed shops, and check out the historic Akaroa Lighthouse. Swim at Akaroa Beach if the weather permits. This is a beautiful, budget-friendly afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Christchurch by late afternoon/early evening bus. Cook a simple pasta dinner back at the resort using supermarket supplies. Review tomorrow's plans for the journey south.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort — oats or toast with spreads (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch from supermarket supplies — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks to eat at Akaroa waterfront (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with jarred sauce and salad at the resort (~NZD $10-12)

day_by_day.notes: The French Connection bus runs from Christchurch to Akaroa for ~NZD $35 return — book in advance online. Alternatively, rent a car with other travellers to split costs. Bring sunscreen, water, and layers as coastal weather can be unpredictable. Budget for the day: ~NZD $55-65.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and begin the scenic drive south toward Lake Tekapo (approximately 3.5 hours). If without a car, take the Intercity bus from Christchurch to Lake Tekapo (~NZD $25-35). Stop at Geraldine on the way for a short stretch and to visit the free Talbot Forest Scenic Reserve for a quick bush walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Tekapo. Check into a budget hostel (YHA Lake Tekapo or Tailor Made Tekapo Hostel, ~NZD $30-40 per night in a dorm). Then head straight to the famous Church of the Good Shepherd for photos — it's free and iconic. Hike up Mount John via the free walking track (2-3 hours return) for breathtaking 360-degree views of the turquoise lake and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Lake Tekapo is one of the world's best stargazing locations (Dark Sky Reserve). Join a budget-friendly self-guided stargazing session from the lakeside — completely free. The Milky Way is often visible with the naked eye in November.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort before checkout (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat en route or at Geraldine — supermarket supplies (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Cook at the hostel kitchen — buy pasta, vegetables, and sauce from the local Four Square supermarket (~NZD $12-15)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Tekapo is a must-visit for stargazing — November skies are excellent. The Mount John hike is free and one of the best viewpoints in the South Island. Book hostel accommodation in advance as Tekapo gets busy. Budget for the day: ~NZD $70-90 including transport and accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for sunrise at Lake Tekapo — the pink and orange hues reflecting off the turquoise lake are absolutely magical and completely free. Then hike the Tekapo Canal Walk (approximately 2 hours, flat and easy) along the hydro canal with stunning mountain views. Stop at the Cowan's Hill Lookout track for additional panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel south to Twizel (about 45 minutes) and then on to Mount Cook Village (Aoraki) — approximately 1.5 hours from Tekapo. Check into the YHA Aoraki Mount Cook (~NZD $35-45 dorm). Begin the Kea Point Track — a free, 2-hour return hike to the terminal face of the Mueller Glacier with stunning views of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mount Cook Village. Cook dinner at the hostel. Enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery as the alpenglow turns the peaks golden at sunset. Stargaze again — Aoraki is also a Dark Sky Reserve.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Tekapo hostel — cereal or toast (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kea Point or en route (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Hostel kitchen dinner — stir-fry with rice and vegetables from Twizel New World supermarket (~NZD $12)

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on groceries in Twizel before heading to Mount Cook as the only shop at the village is very expensive. The Kea Point Track is free and highly recommended. Bring warm layers as Mount Cook can be cold even in November. Budget for the day: ~NZD $60-80.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. Start early with the Hooker Valley Track — New Zealand's most popular day hike and completely free. This 3-hour return walk crosses three swing bridges and ends at the Hooker Glacier Lake with floating icebergs and jaw-dropping views of Mount Cook. Start by 7-8am to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Hooker Valley Track, rest and refuel at the hostel. If energy allows, attempt the Red Tarns Track (1.5 hours return) for elevated views over the village and surrounding peaks. Alternatively, visit the free Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre museum exhibit at The Hermitage (the museum portion is free).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hostel. Cook a hearty dinner to refuel from the day's hiking. Chat with fellow travellers and plan the journey to Queenstown. Enjoy the silence and stars of the national park.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — oats with honey and banana (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the Hooker Glacier Lake — sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Hostel kitchen — lentil soup with bread, hearty and budget-friendly (~NZD $10)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is arguably the best free hike in New Zealand — do not miss it. Start early to avoid crowds and for the best light. Bring plenty of water and snacks. Weather can change rapidly — check the MetService forecast the night before. Budget for the day: ~NZD $30-40 (mostly food and hostel).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mount Cook and travel to Queenstown via the Lindis Pass (approximately 4 hours). The drive through the Lindis Pass is stunning — golden tussock-covered hills and wide open skies. Stop at the Lindis Pass summit for photos and a short stretch walk. Arrive in Queenstown late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a budget hostel in Queenstown (Base Backpackers, Nomads Queenstown, or YHA Queenstown Lakefront — ~NZD $35-50 dorm). Explore Queenstown's free attractions: walk along Lake Wakatipu waterfront, visit the free Queenstown Gardens (rose gardens and disc golf course), and hike up to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2-3 hours return, free) for panoramic views over the lake and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant but budget-friendly dining scene. Stroll the waterfront and watch the sunset over The Remarkables. Visit the Queenstown Night Market (Thursday-Sunday) for cheap, delicious street food from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Mount Cook hostel before departure (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lindis Pass or upon arrival in Queenstown (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market — try various stalls for ~NZD $15-20 total (dumplings, crepes, curries, etc.)

day_by_day.notes: If travelling by bus, Intercity runs Twizel to Queenstown for ~NZD $30-45. If renting a car, the Lindis Pass route is far more scenic than the highway. Book Queenstown hostel well in advance — it's extremely popular. Budget for the day: ~NZD $80-100 including transport and accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: BUNGEE JUMPING DAY! Head to AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy — the world's first commercial bungee jumping site, just 23km from Queenstown. The 43-metre jump over the stunning Kawarau Gorge is an absolute bucket-list experience (~NZD $205). Book online in advance for the best price. Arrive early for the first jump of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, recover with a free walk along the Kawarau River trail near the bridge. Return to Queenstown and take the free Queenstown Hill Walk or relax at the lakefront. Visit the free Queenstown Museum at the Eichardt's Library for local history.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump! Head to Fergburger — Queenstown's legendary and surprisingly affordable burger joint (~NZD $15-18 for a massive burger). Join other backpackers at the hostel common room or visit one of the free live music venues on the strip.

meals.breakfast: Light self-catered breakfast before the jump — don't eat too much! Toast and banana (~NZD $4)
meals.lunch: Supermarket wrap or sandwich post-jump (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Fergburger — the iconic Queenstown experience (~NZD $16-18)

day_by_day.notes: Book AJ Hackett Kawarau Bungy online at least 2-3 days in advance for the best rates and your preferred time slot. The jump includes a certificate and basic viewing for spectators is free. This is the biggest expense of the trip but worth every cent. Budget for the day: ~NZD $240-260.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Routeburn Track Day Hike — one of New Zealand's Great Walks and an absolute highlight of the South Island. Take the early morning shuttle from Queenstown to the Routeburn Flats trailhead (~NZD $35-45 return with Tracknet or similar). Hike from the Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Flats and Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4 hours one way, 8km). The track winds through ancient beech forest, past waterfalls, and opens to stunning alpine meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Routeburn Falls Hut for lunch with incredible views. Begin the return hike back to the trailhead, taking in the scenery from a different perspective. The full day hike is approximately 16km return and takes 6-8 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Return shuttle to Queenstown. Arrive back tired but exhilarated. Cook a simple dinner at the hostel or grab cheap takeaways. Rest your legs — you've earned it!

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at hostel before shuttle (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Routeburn Falls Hut — sandwiches, energy bars, and fruit (~NZD $10)
meals.dinner: Hostel kitchen — simple pasta or rice dish (~NZD $10-12)

day_by_day.notes: This is the featured Routeburn Track Day Hike experience. Book the Tracknet shuttle in advance as spots fill quickly. Wear proper hiking boots, bring rain gear, plenty of water (2L minimum), and sunscreen. The track is well-marked. Check Department of Conservation (DOC) website for current track conditions. Budget for the day: ~NZD $65-80.

day_by_day.morning: Rest your legs with a gentler morning activity. Hike the Ben Lomond Track — start with the Tiki Trail from central Queenstown (free) up through native bush to the Ben Lomond Saddle. The saddle alone (2-3 hours return from town) offers incredible views and is free. For the full summit, allow 5-6 hours return.
day_by_day.afternoon: If you took the shorter saddle option, spend the afternoon exploring Arrowtown — a charming gold rush-era village 20km from Queenstown (free Arrow River walk, free Chinese settlement historic site, free museum). Take the Orbus bus from Queenstown (~NZD $3 with Bee Card).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for sunset at the lakefront. Visit the free Queenstown waterfront and watch the TSS Earnslaw steamship return to port. Grab cheap fish and chips from a local takeaway shop for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel — eggs on toast (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the hike or Arrowtown bakery for a cheap pie (~NZD $6-8)
meals.dinner: Fish and chips from a local takeaway — classic New Zealand meal (~NZD $12-15)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Lomond Saddle is free and the views rival the gondola (which costs ~NZD $50+). Arrowtown is a wonderful free half-day trip with genuine gold rush history. The Bee Card for Orbus buses saves money on local transport. Budget for the day: ~NZD $30-40.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown and travel to Wanaka (approximately 1 hour by bus or car via the Crown Range — the highest sealed road in New Zealand, with stunning views). Check into a budget hostel in Wanaka (Wanaka Backpaka or YHA Wanaka, ~NZD $30-40 dorm). Begin the Roy's Peak Track — a challenging but iconic 16km return hike with 1,200m elevation gain. Start early (by 7am) to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Roy's Peak hike — the summit at 1,578m offers one of the most photographed views in New Zealand, with Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring National Park spread out below. The famous 'Instagram ridge' photo spot is near the top. Allow 5-6 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Descend back to Wanaka, tired but triumphant. Explore Wanaka's charming lakefront. Visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — a lone willow tree growing in the lake, perfect for sunset photos (free). Cook dinner at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before the hike (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Roy's Peak summit — enjoy the views! (~NZD $10)
meals.dinner: Hostel kitchen — budget stir-fry with noodles and vegetables (~NZD $10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is closed from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season — it reopens in mid-November, so timing is perfect for this trip. Start very early to avoid the crowds and midday heat. Bring at least 2L of water as there is no water on the track. The Crown Range road is breathtaking — stop at the summit lookout. Budget for the day: ~NZD $60-75.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wanaka's free and low-cost attractions. Hike the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop Track (2-3 hours, free) — a stunning circuit through farmland and forest with elevated views of Lake Wanaka and Roys Peak. The track starts just 7km from Wanaka town centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Puzzling World (~NZD $17-20 entry) — a quirky attraction with optical illusions and a famous tilted building that's worth the budget splurge. Alternatively, swim at Wanaka Beach (free) and kayak or paddleboard rental (~NZD $25-30 per hour). Explore the Wanaka lakefront on a free bike ride (hire a bike for ~NZD $15-20 for a half day).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Wanaka. Watch the sunset over Lake Wanaka from the lakefront — it's magical and free. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at Francesca's Italian Kitchen or grab a cheap pizza from a local spot to celebrate the penultimate evening of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel (~NZD $5)
meals.lunch: Supermarket wrap or sandwich eaten at the lake (~NZD $8)
meals.dinner: Budget pizza or pasta at a local Wanaka eatery (~NZD $18-22)

day_by_day.notes: The Diamond Lake Track is far less crowded than Roy's Peak and equally beautiful. Wanaka is a wonderful town to simply wander — the lakefront is free and stunning. If budget allows, Puzzling World is a fun afternoon activity. Budget for the day: ~NZD $50-65.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Wanaka. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the Lake Wanaka waterfront and a final photo of That Wanaka Tree in the morning light. Grab a coffee from a local café as a treat. Pack up and check out of the hostel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel back toward Christchurch (approximately 4.5-5 hours via State Highway 8 through the Mackenzie Basin — scenic route past Lake Tekapo and Lake Pukaki with Mount Cook views). Stop at Lake Pukaki viewpoint for iconic Mount Cook reflection photos (free). If time allows, stop at Lake Tekapo again for one last look.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Christchurch. Depending on your departure flight details, either check back into accommodation or head to the airport. Spend your last New Zealand dollars on a final meal at a Christchurch restaurant or café. Reflect on an incredible 13-day South Island adventure!

meals.breakfast: Café treat for the last morning — flat white and toast at a Wanaka café (~NZD $12-15)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route to Christchurch (~NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Christchurch restaurant — try Hello Sunday brunch spot or Riverside Market for varied, affordable options (~NZD $18-25)

day_by_day.notes: The Lake Pukaki viewpoint with Mount Cook reflection is one of the most stunning free photo spots in New Zealand — do not skip it. Fill the rental car with petrol before returning if you hired one. Allow extra time for the drive back to Christchurch as the scenery will tempt you to stop frequently. Total trip budget estimate: ~NZD $1,200-1,500 for 13 days including accommodation, transport, food, and key activities. Budget for the day: ~NZD $60-80.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack from airport or a 24-hour convenience store near the resort — grab a sandwich, fruit, and drinks to unwind in your room.

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival at 22:30, no activities are scheduled. Confirm your resort transfer in advance. Pack a small carry-on snack for the journey. Rest well — the adventure begins tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. After breakfast, take a relaxing stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Explore the local waterfront area, breathe in the coastal air, and visit a nearby lookout point for scenic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into central Christchurch for an orientation afternoon. Visit the Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free entry) and stroll through the regenerating city centre. Explore the vibrant arts and food precinct at The Tannery or Little High Eatery.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Christchurch city centre. Return to the resort for an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort's beachfront café — enjoy eggs, toast, and fresh juice while overlooking the ocean.
meals.lunch: Little High Eatery in Christchurch — a mid-range food hall with diverse options including burgers, noodles, and fresh salads (NZD $15–25 per person).
meals.dinner: Fiddlesticks Restaurant & Bar in Christchurch — a well-regarded mid-range spot with a seasonal New Zealand menu. Budget NZD $35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day. No strenuous activity planned. Pick up any hiking or adventure gear you may need at Christchurch outdoor stores like Kathmandu or Bivouac Outdoor.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Christchurch early and drive south along the scenic State Highway 1, then inland toward Lake Tekapo (approx. 3 hours). Stop at Tekapo Springs for a lakeside walk. Visit the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd and enjoy panoramic views of the turquoise glacier-fed lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive south to Queenstown (approx. 3 hours from Tekapo). Stop at Lindis Pass for dramatic high-country tundra scenery. Arrive in Queenstown by late afternoon. Check into local accommodation for the next several nights while using Queenstown as your adventure base.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's buzzing lakefront and town centre. Browse the shops along the Mall and enjoy your first Queenstown dinner with views of the Remarkables mountain range.

meals.breakfast: Grab a hearty breakfast at a Christchurch café before departure — try Café Valentino or a local bakery for pastries and coffee.
meals.lunch: Stop at Tekapo's Kohan Japanese Restaurant or Mackenzie's Bar & Grill overlooking the lake — mid-range, NZD $20–35.
meals.dinner: Fergburger in Queenstown — the legendary iconic burger joint. Expect a queue but absolutely worth it. Budget NZD $15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a driving day — approximately 5–6 hours total. Rent a car in Christchurch for maximum flexibility. Fill up fuel before leaving Tekapo as stations are sparse on the route. Queenstown will be your base for Days 3–8.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump — the world's first commercial bungee site, a thrilling 43-metre plunge above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. Arrive early (from 9:00am) to beat the crowds. Watch others jump while you prepare, then take the plunge!
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, drive the scenic Gibbston Valley wine route (the 'Valley of the Vines'). Visit a local winery such as Amisfield or Peregrine Wines for a cellar door tasting — a perfect contrast to the morning's excitement.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Stroll along the lakefront at sunset and enjoy dinner with views of Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown — try The Cow restaurant for eggs and coffee, or grab a takeaway from a local café before heading to Kawarau.
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery Restaurant — enjoy a platter of local cheeses, charcuterie, and wood-fired food paired with a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir. NZD $30–45.
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Josh Emett in Queenstown — a celebrated mid-to-upscale New Zealand dining experience. Book ahead. NZD $45–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump in advance through AJ Hackett Bungy NZ. Cost approx. NZD $195–235 per person. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. Photos and video packages are available at additional cost.

day_by_day.morning: Take on the Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungee at a breathtaking 134 metres above the remote Nevis River gorge. A bus transfer from Queenstown takes you to this remote and dramatic location. The experience includes a suspended cable car ride to the jump platform.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Recover with a relaxing cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship to Walter Peak High Country Farm. Enjoy the mountain scenery from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farm-to-table dinner at Walter Peak Farm (included with some Earnslaw cruise packages) or return to Queenstown for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Queenstown accommodation or a quick stop at Vudu Café & Larder — great coffee and fresh baked goods.
meals.lunch: Pack a hearty lunch from a Queenstown deli or supermarket to eat at the Nevis site — facilities are limited at the remote location.
meals.dinner: Walter Peak Farm Colonel's Homestead Restaurant (if taking the dinner cruise) — a buffet of New Zealand lamb, salmon, and seasonal vegetables. NZD $99–130 including cruise. Alternatively, try Bao Bei Queenstown for Asian fusion at NZD $25–40.

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy is operated by AJ Hackett. Cost approx. NZD $275 per person. Minimum weight 45kg, maximum 127kg. Book well in advance. The bus transfer from Queenstown is included. This is a full adrenaline day — the afternoon cruise provides perfect recovery time.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Routeburn Track Day Hike — one of New Zealand's Great Walks. Take a shuttle from Queenstown to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead. Hike through ancient beech forests, past crystal-clear streams, and up to the breathtaking Routeburn Falls (approx. 4 hours return to the falls).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking if energy allows, or begin the return journey back to the trailhead. The alpine scenery — open tussock flats, towering peaks, and glacial valleys — is spectacular in November's early summer light.
day_by_day.evening: Return shuttle to Queenstown by late afternoon. Rest tired legs and enjoy a quiet evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your accommodation or grab a packed breakfast from a local café before the shuttle departs.
meals.lunch: Pack your own trail lunch — sandwiches, energy bars, nuts, fruit, and plenty of water. There are no facilities on the track.
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant in Queenstown — a cosy, intimate mid-range spot with excellent New Zealand cuisine. NZD $35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Routeburn Track shuttle through Tracknet or Queenstown's i-SITE visitor centre. Wear sturdy hiking boots and layers — alpine weather can change rapidly even in November. Carry rain gear. The hike to Routeburn Falls is approximately 8km return and rated moderate.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a well-earned rest morning in Queenstown. Sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and explore the Queenstown Gardens — a peaceful lakeside park perfect for a gentle stroll and recovery after two big adventure days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and the Remarkables. Try the luge rides at the top for some lighthearted fun, or simply enjoy the views and a coffee at the Skyline Restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant nightlife scene — visit Ballarat Trading Company for craft beers or enjoy cocktails at Zephyr Bar. This is your last evening in Queenstown before heading to Fiordland.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Bespoke Kitchen — a beloved local café known for wholesome, fresh food and great coffee. NZD $18–28.
meals.lunch: Skyline Restaurant at the top of the gondola — buffet lunch with panoramic views. NZD $45–55 per person (gondola + lunch combo available).
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill Queenstown — fresh New Zealand seafood in a relaxed setting. Try the Bluff oysters or blue cod. NZD $35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Gondola ticket approx. NZD $32 adults (views only). Use today to repack your bag for the Milford Track multi-day hike starting tomorrow. Ensure you have your Great Walk booking confirmation, hut passes, and appropriate gear. Check weather forecasts for Fiordland.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early and drive to Te Anau (approx. 2 hours) — the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check in at Te Anau for one night before the Milford Track begins. Visit the DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to confirm your Great Walk booking and get a trail briefing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township. Take a short walk along the Te Anau lakefront or visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by boat (approx. 2 hours, NZD $80 per person) — a magical underground experience with thousands of glowworms.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a hearty pre-hike dinner in Te Anau to fuel up for the Milford Track ahead.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Queenstown accommodation before departure, or stop at a café en route.
meals.lunch: Miles Better Pies in Te Anau — a local favourite for hearty NZ pies, sandwiches, and snacks. NZD $8–15.
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — a charming mid-range restaurant in a historic cottage serving excellent venison, lamb, and local fish. NZD $35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Track Great Walk (Days 9–12) must be pre-booked through DOC (Department of Conservation) well in advance. The guided walk option (approx. NZD $2,595–3,000) includes hut accommodation and a guide. The independent walk (approx. NZD $175 hut fees) requires you to carry your own gear. Confirm your booking type and pack accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the legendary Milford Track Great Walk. Take the ferry from Te Anau Downs to Glade Wharf (the track start). Begin hiking through the pristine Clinton Valley — lush beech forest, clear rivers, and abundant birdlife including kea and fantails. Day 1 covers approximately 5km to Clinton Hut.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Clinton Hut (40 bunks) by early afternoon. Explore the surrounding area, rest, and enjoy the solitude of Fiordland. The hut sits at the edge of the Clinton Valley with stunning mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into hut life — cook your packed dinner on the communal stove, chat with fellow trampers, and enjoy the remarkable silence of one of the world's most pristine wilderness areas. Early bedtime for the longer day ahead.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Te Anau before the ferry — café or self-prepared at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch carried from Te Anau — sandwiches, crackers, cheese, dried fruit, and energy bars.
meals.dinner: Self-prepared hut meal — lightweight dehydrated meals (e.g., Back Country Cuisine), supplemented with snacks and hot drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Track is a 53.5km, 4-day walk. Day 1 is an easy introduction — 5km, mostly flat. Pack rain gear as Fiordland receives extremely high rainfall. The ferry from Te Anau Downs departs at a fixed time — do not be late. No shops or facilities on the track.

day_by_day.morning: Day 2 of the Milford Track: Depart Clinton Hut and hike approximately 16.5km to Mintaro Hut. The trail follows the Clinton River through increasingly dramatic alpine scenery, passing through the Hirere Falls area and climbing gradually toward the MacKinnon Pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mintaro Hut (40 bunks) nestled at the base of the MacKinnon Pass. Rest and explore the surrounding alpine meadows. The scenery becomes more dramatic and open as the valley narrows.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the hut atmosphere, rest sore muscles, and prepare mentally for tomorrow's challenging MacKinnon Pass crossing — the highlight of the entire Milford Track.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at Clinton Hut — oats, muesli, or dehydrated breakfast packs with coffee or tea.
meals.lunch: Trail lunch eaten on the track — packed food carried from Te Anau.
meals.dinner: Dehydrated hut meal at Mintaro Hut — hot meal, hot drinks, and energy-dense snacks.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is moderate in difficulty — 16.5km with some elevation gain toward the end. Pace yourself. The weather in Fiordland is notoriously changeable — be prepared for rain at any time. November is early summer and generally good for hiking, but conditions can shift quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Day 3 of the Milford Track — the most spectacular day. Cross the iconic MacKinnon Pass (1,154m) with breathtaking 360-degree views of the surrounding Fiordland peaks. Descend steeply into the Arthur Valley via the dramatic Roaring Burn waterfall and pass the stunning Sutherland Falls (580m — one of the world's tallest waterfalls).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent through lush rainforest to Dumpling Hut (40 bunks) — approximately 21km total for the day. This is the longest and most rewarding day on the track.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the MacKinnon Pass crossing with fellow trampers at Dumpling Hut. Share stories, treat tired feet, and enjoy the satisfaction of completing the track's most iconic section.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at Mintaro Hut before the pass crossing — essential to fuel the biggest day.
meals.lunch: Pack extra snacks and lunch for this long day — eat at the MacKinnon Pass shelter or at Sutherland Falls.
meals.dinner: Dehydrated hut meal at Dumpling Hut — extra calories well earned today.

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 is the most challenging — 21km with significant elevation gain and descent. Start early. If weather closes in on the pass, DOC rangers may advise on safety. The side trip to Sutherland Falls (1 hour return) is highly recommended and not to be missed. Poles recommended for the steep descent.

day_by_day.morning: Day 4 (final day) of the Milford Track: Depart Dumpling Hut and hike the final 18km through the Arthur Valley to Sandfly Point. The trail passes through magnificent rainforest, crosses swing bridges, and follows the Arthur River to the Milford Sound foreshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive triumphantly at Sandfly Point — the end of the Milford Track. Take the ferry across to Milford Sound. Celebrate your achievement with a scenic cruise on Milford Sound — one of the world's most dramatic fiords, with sheer cliff faces, cascading waterfalls, and resident dolphins and seals.
day_by_day.evening: Board the coach transfer from Milford Sound back to Te Anau (approx. 2.5 hours). Check into Te Anau accommodation, shower, and enjoy a well-deserved celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast at Dumpling Hut — eat well for the last day's walk.
meals.lunch: Eat remaining trail food on the track or grab a snack at the Milford Sound visitor facilities.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Ristorante Pizzeria Da Toto in Te Anau — a local favourite for hearty Italian food after a big adventure. NZD $25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound cruise is bookable through Real Journeys or Go Orange — approx. NZD $85–120 per person. The coach transfer back to Te Anau is essential to book in advance. You will have completed one of the world's greatest walks — a huge achievement!

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau and drive back toward Christchurch (or your departure point) via the scenic Queenstown route. Stop at Queenstown for a final coffee and browse of the town. Alternatively, if flying out of Queenstown, enjoy a final morning lakefront walk and last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive north if heading to Christchurch (approx. 4–5 hours from Queenstown). Stop at Lake Pukaki for the iconic Aoraki/Mount Cook reflection view — one of New Zealand's most photographed landscapes. Arrive in Christchurch by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for your final night. Enjoy a sunset walk along the beachfront, reflect on 13 incredible days, and enjoy a farewell dinner with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Te Anau before departure — try Miles Better Pies or your accommodation café.
meals.lunch: Stop at Queenstown for lunch — revisit Fergburger for a final legendary burger, or try a lakefront café.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beachfront restaurant near Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh New Zealand seafood and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir to toast an unforgettable South Island adventure. Budget NZD $40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is your final day — allow plenty of time for the drive and stops. If flying home from Christchurch the next day, confirm your flight time and arrange an airport transfer. Consider posting or couriering any heavy hiking gear home rather than carrying it through the airport. What a trip — Milford Track, two world-class bungee jumps, Routeburn Track, and the best of the South Island!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of the world's greatest walks through Fiordland National Park, passing stunning waterfalls, alpine meadows, and dramatic mountain passes. The 53.5km trail takes 4 days and offers breathtaking scenery including the famous Mackinnon Pass at 1154m elevation.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungee jumping site, a 43-metre jump above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. This iconic experience is operated by AJ Hackett and includes the option to touch the water on your jump for an extra thrill.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the legendary Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's Great Walks, winding through ancient beech forests, alpine lakes, and panoramic mountain ridges shared between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The Routeburn Falls section is particularly spectacular.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Join a guided hike on the famous Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers descending into a temperate rainforest. Explore stunning ice caves, seracs, and crevasses with expert guides who provide all necessary equipment including crampons and ice axes.
experiences.location: Franz Josef Glacier Village, West Coast

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungee jump at 134 metres above the remote Nevis River gorge. This extreme freefall lasts 8.5 seconds and reaches speeds of 120km/h, offering unmatched adrenaline and jaw-dropping views of the Central Otago landscape from the suspended cable car pod.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night supper at the resort's 24-hour in-room dining — charcuterie board, artisan cheeses, and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir to welcome you to New Zealand.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — no activities scheduled before 22:30. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request a late check-in amenity with the resort in advance. Rest and recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. After a late-night arrival, take a slow morning on your private beachfront balcony. Enjoy a full gourmet breakfast at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant overlooking the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation drive and exploration of the surrounding coastal area near the resort. Visit a local artisan market or boutique wine shop to pick up regional South Island wines and handcrafted souvenirs. Alternatively, enjoy the resort's spa with a 90-minute deep-tissue or hot stone massage to recover from jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a premium dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant. Enjoy New Zealand king salmon, Canterbury lamb, and locally sourced seasonal produce paired with a curated wine flight.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit platters, artisan pastries, and freshly brewed single-origin coffee.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled seafood platter with lemon aioli, fresh garden salad, and sparkling water or local craft beer.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant — Canterbury rack of lamb with rosemary jus, roasted root vegetables, and a Central Otago Pinot Noir pairing.

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day after your late arrival. Take it easy and allow yourself to adjust to the time zone. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic helicopter flight from a nearby helipad to Franz Josef Glacier on the West Coast. Begin your guided Franz Josef Glacier Hike — a world-class experience walking through ice caves, seracs, and towering blue-ice formations with a certified glacier guide. Full safety gear and crampons provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the glacier hike through the upper ice fields with breathtaking views of the Southern Alps. Descend back to the glacier base and enjoy a hot debrief with your guide. Explore the Franz Josef township briefly before your private helicopter return transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxing evening with a private beachfront bonfire experience arranged by the resort, complete with champagne and canapés under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — smashed avocado on sourdough, poached eggs, fresh juice, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the resort and enjoyed at the glacier base — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, premium chocolate, and a thermos of hot tea or coffee.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience at the resort — New Zealand crayfish (rock lobster) with drawn butter, truffle fries, and a chilled Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc.

day_by_day.notes: The Franz Josef Glacier Hike requires moderate fitness. Weather conditions on the West Coast can change rapidly — helicopter flights may be subject to weather delays. Wear layered clothing and waterproof gear. Confirm helicopter transfer with the resort concierge the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury vehicle transfer toward Queenstown (approximately 4–5 hours via the scenic Southern Alps route). Stop at Haast Pass for a short nature walk and waterfall viewing — the Fantail Falls and Thunder Creek Falls are spectacular and easily accessible from the roadside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive through the Haast Pass World Heritage Area, stopping at Lake Wanaka for a lakeside lunch. Explore the charming Wanaka township — visit galleries, boutique shops, and the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' for photos. Continue to Queenstown and check into a luxury Queenstown property (arranged as a satellite stay by the resort concierge).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Queenstown and settle into your luxury Queenstown accommodation. Stroll along the Queenstown waterfront at dusk with views over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range. Pre-dinner cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the lake.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — full cooked breakfast with eggs, bacon, grilled tomato, mushrooms, and freshly squeezed juice.
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at a premium restaurant in Wanaka — seared South Island venison, roasted seasonal vegetables, and a glass of local Pinot Noir.
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Queenstown at a top-rated restaurant — tasting menu featuring New Zealand beef tenderloin, Bluff oysters, and an expertly curated wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from the resort area to Queenstown via Haast Pass is one of New Zealand's most scenic routes — allow extra time for photo stops. Ensure the luxury vehicle is pre-booked with a private driver. Confirm Queenstown accommodation arrangements with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump — head to the iconic Kawarau Gorge, the birthplace of commercial bungee jumping. Take the legendary 43-metre plunge above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. This historic site offers a thrilling yet iconic experience. Optional: upgrade to a tandem jump or watch from the dedicated viewing platform.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-adrenaline recovery with a private wine tasting tour through the Gibbston Valley — known as the 'Valley of Vines,' this stunning gorge is home to world-class Pinot Noir producers. Visit 2–3 boutique wineries with a guided tasting and cheese pairing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a luxury evening. Enjoy a private gondola ride up Bob's Peak for panoramic sunset views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu, followed by dinner at the Skyline restaurant with 360-degree mountain and lake views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Queenstown — eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and barista coffee.
meals.lunch: Winery lunch during the Gibbston Valley tour — artisan cheese and charcuterie boards paired with estate Pinot Noir and Riesling.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Skyline Queenstown's premium restaurant — New Zealand lamb, local seafood, and dessert with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungee Jump in advance through AJ Hackett Bungy — early morning slots are recommended to beat crowds. The Gibbston Valley wine tour can be arranged through the concierge with a private driver ensuring no drink-driving concerns.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — experience New Zealand's most extreme bungee jump at a heart-stopping 134 metres above the remote Nevis River gorge. A dedicated shuttle takes you to the suspended gondola platform. This is a bucket-list adrenaline experience not for the faint-hearted. Minimum age 10, minimum weight 45kg.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ultimate adrenaline rush, unwind with a private luxury jet boat experience on the Shotover River — carving through narrow canyons at high speed. Alternatively, opt for a serene private lake cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a luxury charter vessel with champagne service.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a premium spa treatment at one of Queenstown's luxury day spas — choose from a couples' massage, hot stone therapy, or a full body wrap. Conclude the evening with a premium dinner at one of Queenstown's most celebrated fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast before the Nevis jump — full cooked breakfast with high-protein options: eggs, avocado, grilled meats, and strong coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-jump celebration lunch in Queenstown town centre — premium burger and craft beer at a top gastropub, or sushi and sashimi at a high-end Japanese restaurant.
meals.dinner: Degustation dinner at Queenstown's finest restaurant — 7-course tasting menu with matched wines, featuring the best of New Zealand's seasonal produce.

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy Jump requires pre-booking through AJ Hackett Bungy Queenstown. The shuttle departs from central Queenstown. Participants must be in good health — check medical requirements in advance. This is the highest bungee jump of the trip, so ensure it is scheduled on a day with good weather forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Day Hike — depart early via private transfer to the Routeburn Track trailhead near Glenorchy (approximately 45 minutes from Queenstown). Begin hiking one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, winding through ancient beech forests, alpine meadows, and past cascading waterfalls with dramatic mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Routeburn Track day hike, ascending to higher alpine terrain with sweeping views over the Dart Valley and surrounding peaks. Enjoy your packed gourmet picnic lunch at a scenic viewpoint. Descend and return to the trailhead by private transfer back to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening in Queenstown. Enjoy a soak in a private hot tub or resort spa pool. Light pre-dinner drinks at a lakeside bar, followed by a premium dinner showcasing Queenstown's thriving culinary scene.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at the hotel — porridge with honey and berries, eggs, toast, and coffee to fuel the day's hiking.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic lunch on the Routeburn Track — premium wraps, energy bars, fresh fruit, trail mix, and a thermos of hot soup or coffee.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top Queenstown restaurant — wood-fired South Island venison, truffle risotto, and a bottle of Central Otago Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track day hike covers approximately 10–16 km depending on the section chosen. Wear sturdy hiking boots, carry rain gear, and apply sunscreen. The track can be muddy after rain. Book the private transfer to Glenorchy in advance. This is a moderate-to-challenging hike — confirm fitness levels before committing to the full day section.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown for Te Anau via private luxury vehicle (approximately 2 hours). Check in to a premium Te Anau lodge. This is the gateway to Fiordland National Park. After settling in, take a scenic walk along the Te Anau lakefront and explore the charming township.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a magical underground world of limestone caves illuminated by thousands of tiny glowworms. The tour includes a boat ride through the cave system on the shores of Lake Te Anau. This is a truly unique and otherworldly experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Te Anau aboard a private charter vessel with champagne and canapés, watching the alpenglow light up the Fiordland mountains. Dinner at the lodge's premium restaurant overlooking the lake.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the Queenstown hotel before departure — smoked salmon bagels, fresh fruit, yogurt, and barista coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Te Anau after arrival — premium café lunch featuring local venison pie, fresh salads, and homemade desserts.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Te Anau lodge restaurant — pan-seared blue cod with lemon caper butter, roasted vegetables, and a Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc.

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is the base for the Milford Track Great Walk beginning tomorrow. Ensure all hiking gear, permits, and guided walk arrangements are confirmed. Pack bags for a multi-day hike — leave non-essential luggage securely at the lodge. The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour should be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the legendary Milford Track Great Walk — one of the world's finest walks. Depart Te Anau by private boat across Lake Te Anau to the trailhead at Glade Wharf. Begin hiking through the serene Clinton Valley, surrounded by ancient beech forest, crystal-clear rivers, and towering peaks. Stay in premium guided walk huts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Clinton River through lush Fiordland rainforest. Arrive at Clinton Hut (guided walk) for the first night on the track. Enjoy the extraordinary silence and wilderness of Fiordland National Park. Afternoon free to explore the surroundings, birdwatch for kea and fantails, and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner prepared by the guided walk hut staff — hearty, high-quality meals served in the communal dining area. Evening briefing by the guide on the next day's route. Star-gazing from the hut deck in one of New Zealand's darkest sky areas.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Te Anau lodge before departure — full cooked breakfast to fuel the first day of hiking.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Milford Track — premium sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, and a thermos of hot soup provided by the guided walk operator.
meals.dinner: Hut dinner on the Milford Track — hearty New Zealand-style meal with soup, main course, and dessert prepared by hut staff.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Track guided walk is a 4-day, 53.5 km journey. Only guided walk participants can stay in the premium guided huts. The guided walk is fully catered with meals and accommodation included. Ensure all gear is packed the night before — waterproof jacket, sturdy boots, and warm layers are essential. Sandflies are prevalent in Fiordland — bring high-DEET insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Day 2 of the Milford Track — depart Clinton Hut and hike through the stunning upper Clinton Valley. The trail ascends gradually toward Mintaro Hut, passing through increasingly dramatic alpine scenery. Cross swing bridges over glacial rivers and look out for rare Fiordland wildlife including kea parrots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the ascent toward the iconic Mackinnon Pass — the high point of the Milford Track at 1,154 metres. The views from the pass on a clear day are absolutely spectacular, overlooking both the Clinton and Arthur Valleys. Descend to Mintaro Hut for the second night.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mintaro Hut in the late afternoon. Rest aching legs, enjoy a hot shower, and gather with fellow hikers for the evening meal. The guide provides a fascinating talk on the history and geology of the Milford Track.

meals.breakfast: Hut breakfast at Clinton Hut — porridge, toast, eggs, and hot drinks to fuel the big day ahead.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at Mackinnon Pass — sandwiches, snacks, and hot drinks with panoramic alpine views.
meals.dinner: Hut dinner at Mintaro Hut — a hearty, warming meal after a long day of hiking, with soup, main, and dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The Mackinnon Pass section is the most challenging part of the Milford Track. Weather at the pass can be severe — be prepared for wind, rain, and cold even in November. The guided walk operators will advise on conditions. This is one of the most rewarding days of the entire trip — pace yourself on the ascent.

day_by_day.morning: Day 3 of the Milford Track — depart Mintaro Hut and descend into the Arthur Valley. Pass the spectacular Sutherland Falls — one of New Zealand's highest waterfalls at 580 metres — with an optional side trail to the base of the falls for a truly awe-inspiring experience. The descent through lush rainforest is dramatic and beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Arthur Valley through ancient rainforest draped in moss and ferns. Cross multiple swing bridges and enjoy the increasingly dramatic scenery as the valley narrows toward Milford Sound. Arrive at Dumpling Hut for the final night on the track.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate night on the Milford Track with fellow hikers and guides. Share stories of the journey over a well-earned dinner. The guide provides a briefing on the final day's route to Milford Sound.

meals.breakfast: Hut breakfast at Mintaro Hut — full cooked breakfast to fuel the long descent day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed near Sutherland Falls — a memorable picnic spot beside one of New Zealand's most iconic natural wonders.
meals.dinner: Hut dinner at Dumpling Hut — celebratory meal with the group to mark the near-completion of the legendary track.

day_by_day.notes: The side trail to the base of Sutherland Falls adds approximately 30–40 minutes to the day but is highly recommended. Sandflies are particularly prevalent in the Arthur Valley — keep insect repellent accessible. The final stretch to Dumpling Hut can be muddy — trekking poles are very helpful.

day_by_day.morning: Final day of the Milford Track — depart Dumpling Hut for the last leg of the journey to Sandfly Point at Milford Sound. The final section winds through dense rainforest and emerges dramatically at the edge of the fiord. Arrive at Sandfly Point and take in the incredible achievement of completing one of the world's greatest walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a private luxury cruise on Milford Sound — the crown jewel of New Zealand's natural wonders. Sail past towering Mitre Peak, cascading waterfalls, and dramatic fjord walls. Look out for dolphins, fur seals, and rare Fiordland penguins. Enjoy champagne on deck to celebrate completing the Milford Track. Private transfer back to Te Anau and then to Queenstown (or fly by scenic flight).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown or the Aegean Bliss Resort area via private luxury transfer or scenic light aircraft. Celebratory dinner at a premium restaurant to mark the completion of the Milford Track and the adventures of the week.

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast on the Milford Track — full cooked breakfast before the last day's hike.
meals.lunch: Champagne and gourmet canapés aboard the private Milford Sound cruise — celebrating the completion of the Milford Track in spectacular style.
meals.dinner: Grand celebratory dinner at a top-rated restaurant — premium New Zealand beef fillet, fine wines, and a decadent dessert to mark the achievement.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private Milford Sound cruise in advance through the guided walk operator or concierge. The scenic flight option from Milford Sound to Queenstown is highly recommended on a clear day — the aerial views of Fiordland are extraordinary. Ensure luggage left at the Te Anau lodge is collected or transferred.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast on your private beachfront balcony — savour the last moments of your South Island paradise. Take a final leisurely walk along the beach, collect shells, and reflect on an extraordinary 13-day adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell spa treatment at the resort — choose a signature treatment such as a hot stone massage, facial, or hydrotherapy session to ease any post-hiking muscle soreness. Pack, check out, and enjoy one final look at the stunning beachfront before your private transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure flight. Depart New Zealand with extraordinary memories of the South Island's most iconic landscapes, adrenaline experiences, and world-class hospitality.
